key_insight: In low-dimensional pnictogen chalcohalides, surface orientation can shift band edges by up to 0.8 eV even when the most stable facets differ in formation energy by only 0.01–0.03 J m^-2.
engineering_relevance: Facet control is a hidden but critical design variable for achieving efficient charge extraction and higher voltages in MChX solar cells and related photovoltaic devices.
method: First-principles calculations of surface energetics across the full MChX family
Exhaustive crystal-orientation sampling, including low-symmetry facets
Drift-diffusion device simulations for BiSBr to link surface mix to photovoltaic performance
evidence_signal: The study finds (011) and (010) as the most stable terminations in all eight compounds, and device modeling shows mixed facets can lower open-circuit voltage by up to 0.6 V.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on idealized surface and device models, so real-world defects, processing, and interface chemistry may modify the predicted band alignment effects.
paper_title: Surface Physics of Low-Dimensional Pnictogen Chalcohalides and Its Impact on Photovoltaic Technologies
